upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 15 and lives with me here at home. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask:

**Are you responsible for Alex? This typically means either:
- You live with him (which you've mentioned you do), OR
- You're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after him (for example on food, clothes or pocket money)**

Since you mentioned Alex lives with you at home, I assume you're responsible for him, but I just want to confirm this is the case?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. He lives with me and I'm responsible for him - I look after all his needs, pay for his food, clothes, school things, everything really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that. Just a few more questions:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education, such as attending school?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's at school - he's only 15, so he's still doing his GCSEs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently working for 24 hours or more per week, or claiming any benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all - he's focused on his schoolwork. And he doesn't claim any benefits himself either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is Alex currently in hospital or care for an extended period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. He's not in hospital or care - he's at home with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the requirements:

✓ You live in the UK
✓ Alex is 15 years old (under 16)
✓ You're responsible for Alex - he lives with you and you provide for all his needs
✓ Alex is in full-time education
✓ Alex is not working 24+ hours per week or claiming benefits in his own right
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
✓ Alex is not in hospital or care

You can proceed with claiming Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already claimed, you can apply through the official government channels.

**Please note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit itself.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
